mainKeyword: best 4 season tents with stove jacks
guideTitle: Best 4 Season Tents With Stove Jacks (2026)
metaTitle: Best 4 Season Tents With Stove Jacks 2026
metaDescription: A stove jack lets a wood stove vent through the wall of a winter tent. Six four-season tents compared on fabric, snow skirts, size and stove safety.
expertTake: The OneTigris ORBITIS is the pick because it pairs a snow skirt and a stove jack with a lightweight nylon shell sized for four people. The CampRavox is the value pick for two campers who want a basic winter shelter. Anyone who will not tend a fire, carry a carbon monoxide alarm and watch for sparks should skip a stove tent and buy a well-insulated sleeping system instead.
introParagraphs: A hot tent adds a small wood stove to a shelter, and the stove jack is the fire-resistant panel that lets the chimney pass through the wall. It turns a cold camp into a room where you can dry gloves and cook, but only if the tent, stove and habits all match.

Four-season labels are marketing, not a standard. The real questions are what the shell is made of, how much floor area is left once a stove sits inside, whether a snow skirt seals the edges, and how the jack protects the fabric around the pipe.

products.name: OneTigris ORBITIS 4-season hot tent, 4 person, snow skirt

specList.label: Size
specList.value: 13.9 ft long, 8 ft wide, 4.3 ft high

products.description:
The ORBITIS is built around a simple idea: a roomy four-person shelter that still packs like a backpacking tent. The listing gives a footprint of about 13.9 by 8 feet with a 4.3 foot height, and a snow skirt keeps wind and drifting snow out at the edges. The shell is 40D silicone-coated nylon, which is light and sheds water well, with a stove jack included for a tent stove.

The fabric choice shapes how you use it. Silicone-coated nylon can melt from a single hot ember, so a spark arrestor on the chimney and a safe stove distance are not optional. That is a normal tradeoff for the weight savings, and the tent suits people who carry the kit by sled, boat or truck rather than on their back. Next to the VEVOR bell tent, it is far lighter and quicker to pitch, but it gives up the spark tolerance and breathability of a cotton blend.

A detachable footprint protects the floor and makes cleaning easier. Over several winters, watch the seams and the area around the jack, check the pole sleeves for wear and re-seal any weeping stitch lines. Dry the tent fully before storage, because trapped moisture ruins coatings. It earns its place as a general winter tent for small groups.
products.bestFor: Small groups who want a light, roomy winter shelter that handles a stove with snow-skirt weather protection.
pros: Snow skirt blocks drafts and drifting snow
Roomy 13.9 x 8 ft footprint for four people
Light 40D silicone-coated nylon shell
Detachable footprint eases cleaning
cons: Nylon can melt from a stray ember
Stove leaves less usable floor than the label implies
Needs careful drying and seam checks each season

products.name: VEVOR Canvas Bell Tent 4 m, TC fabric, 3 inch stove hole
products.description:
The VEVOR bell tent is a basecamp shelter, not a backpacking tent. It uses TC fabric, a blend of polyester and cotton that breathes better than coated nylon and tolerates sparks better. The 4 meter diameter gives a tall, round interior for up to six people, and the stove hole is a 3 inch flame-resistant port with a 43 by 43 centimeter flap.

The round design is stable in wind because the load spreads around a center pole, but that pole sits in the middle of the floor, so you plan the stove, cots and gear around it. The 3 inch jack suits a smaller stove pipe, which limits the stoves you can use. Compared with the OneTigris ORBITIS, this is a heavy tent that needs a car and a flat site, and it pays you back with comfort and condensation control.

Ownership is the usual canvas routine. Season the fabric before the first trip, dry it completely before packing and ventilate the roof. Mildew is the enemy, and a wet bell tent stored in a bag will be ruined by spring. Inspect the stove jack flap and stitching after every few uses, and keep a patch kit for burn holes.
products.bestFor: Car campers and families who want a roomy, breathable bell tent with a stove hole.
pros: TC fabric breathes and tolerates sparks better
4 m diameter fits up to six people
Flame-resistant 3 inch stove hole with a flap
Tall center for standing room

products.name: Night Cat 8-person instant cabin hot tent, 14 x 8 ft
products.description:
The Night Cat is a family cabin tent that separates sleeping from living. A fully enclosed inner tent sleeps four, and the remaining space works as a living room, which is where a stove would sit. The listing quotes a 14 by 8 foot overall layout with an 80 inch peak and a setup time of about five minutes.

The cabin shape gives vertical walls and a standing-height interior, which suits families and hunting groups. The risk is the stove location: you want it in the living room, well away from the inner tent walls and from anything flammable, and you need a fireproof mat under it. Against the VEVOR bell tent, the Night Cat is quicker to pitch and easier to partition, but it has a more complex frame and a larger wind profile.

In year three, expect to replace zipper sliders and re-tension stakes. Check the poles for bending after wind, seal any seam that leaks and always keep a battery carbon monoxide alarm inside. It is a convenient shelter for groups who want separate sleeping and living areas without a heavy canvas kit.
products.bestFor: Families and hunting parties who want a quick-pitch cabin with a separate sleeping area.

Quick setup of about five minutes

products.name: SHANQUAN inflatable 4-6 person hot tent, 118 x 87 in
products.description:
The SHANQUAN trades poles for air beams. A thickened one-piece PVC air beam frame inflates with a pump, so you skip bent poles and long setup. The 118 by 87 inch floor with a 75 inch height comfortably fits four people, and the stove jack is made from silicone-coated fiberglass fabric, which resists heat better than the tent shell.

Air beams carry a different set of risks than poles. A puncture from a spark or a stake can deflate a beam, and a beam that loses pressure in the cold can sag. That makes it more fragile than a pole tent in a stove environment, so use a spark arrestor and keep the stove at a safe distance. The tent also weighs more and packs bigger than a nylon dome, so it belongs in a vehicle.

Compared with the Night Cat cabin, it sets up in a similar time but has fewer interior partitions. Check the beam valves before each trip, carry a patch kit and a spare pump valve, and re-inflate on cold mornings. If you want a poleless shelter with real stove capability and can accept the weight, it is a convenient choice.
products.bestFor: Campers who prefer pump setup over poles and travel by vehicle.
pros: No poles, air beam frame inflates quickly
Roomy 118 x 87 x 75 inch interior

Fits four to six people
cons: Air beam can be punctured by sparks or stakes

products.name: Naturehike Dune double-layer hot tent with canopy options
products.description:
The Dune is Naturehike's flexible option, with four setups from a fully enclosed overnight mode to open layouts, plus three extra configurations when paired with a canopy. That versatility suits camps where you want a shaded outdoor living area in warm weather and a sealed hot tent in winter. A double layer construction and a stove jack cover the four-season claim.

One drawback is that flexibility adds parts. Extra panels, poles and a canopy mean more to pack, more to lose and more stitching to maintain. A double-layer design also traps warm air, which helps with insulation but invites condensation if you do not vent the top and bottom. Against the simple CampRavox, the Dune offers more options at a higher cost tier.

Ownership favors a tidy camper. Label the poles, keep spare guylines and check the stove jack seam before cold trips. If you travel across seasons and want one tent that can be an open pavilion in summer and a closed stove tent in winter, this is the one.

Double-layer construction adds insulation

products.name: CampRavox 4-season chalet hot tent, 2 adults, 3000 mm
products.description:
The CampRavox is the cheapest way into a stove-ready tent in this lineup. It uses 100 percent 70D ripstop polyester rated to 3000 millimeters, and it fits two adults in a footprint of about 7.4 by 5.25 feet with a 4.25 foot height. Two high-carbon steel poles, ten guylines and thirteen pegs hold it down.

The small size is the catch. Once you place a stove, a firewood pile and two sleeping pads in a space this small, there is little room left and the stove will be uncomfortably close to the walls. Polyester also melts from hot sparks, so a spark arrestor and a conservative stove choice are essential. It suits fast overnight trips with a small stove, not a long winter stay.

In year three, steel poles are the part to watch for bending and rust. Dry the tent before storage and inspect the stitching near the stove jack. Compared with the OneTigris ORBITIS, it is much smaller and much cheaper, which makes it a reasonable pick for a two-person winter overnight.
products.bestFor: Two campers who want the lowest-cost stove-ready winter tent for short trips.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Silicone-coated nylon and polyester shells are light but melt from a single ember, while TC cotton-poly canvas resists sparks and breathes better. The OneTigris ORBITIS and CampRavox use coated synthetics, and the VEVOR bell tent uses TC. If you burn a stove for many hours, spark tolerance matters more than saving a few pounds.

The jack must match your stove pipe diameter, and common openings are 3 to 5 inches, like the VEVOR's 3 inch port with a 43 by 43 cm flap. Place it on a vertical wall or roof panel that clears the stove's minimum distance. A jack protects the pipe exit, not the nearby fabric, so keep a safe gap.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Floor area with a stove inside
buyingCriteria.explanation: A stove, a wood pile and a fireproof mat eat floor space, so an advertised capacity is optimistic. A four-person label often means two people plus a stove. The Night Cat's 14 by 8 foot layout with a separate inner tent solves this better than the 7.4 by 5.25 foot CampRavox.

Cold camping drafts enter at the ground edge, so a snow skirt that you can weigh down with snow improves heat retention. The ORBITIS lists one. Without a skirt, you lose warmth quickly and the stove must work harder.

Wood stoves burn oxygen and can produce carbon monoxide when smoldering or when the chimney drafts poorly. Use a battery alarm inside, vent high and low, and never sleep with a fully loaded stove burning. This applies to every tent in the list, regardless of size.

A 4 m canvas bell tent such as the VEVOR is a vehicle-only shelter, while a nylon dome is manageable on a sled. Inflatable models like the SHANQUAN trade poles for pumps and extra bulk. Match the tent to how you will move it to camp.

Seam tape and thread age. A bead of seam sealer prevents leaks.

faq.q: Is a stove jack the same as a fireproof tent?
faq.a: No. A stove jack protects only the opening where the pipe passes through. The rest of the shell can still melt or burn, so use a spark arrestor, keep the stove well away from walls and never leave it unattended.

faq.q: What stove size should I use in a small tent?
faq.a: A small stove that matches the tent's volume. An oversized stove overheats the space and burns more wood. Check the tent's stove jack diameter and follow the stove's clearance rules.

faq.q: Is canvas better than nylon for a stove tent?
faq.a: Canvas tolerates sparks and breathes, but it is heavy and needs care. Nylon is lighter but melts more easily. The choice depends on how you transport the tent.

faq.q: Do I need a carbon monoxide alarm?
faq.a: Yes. Wood stoves can produce carbon monoxide, which is odorless and deadly. Use a battery alarm, vent the tent high and low and never sleep with a fully loaded stove burning.

faq.q: Can I use these tents without a stove?
faq.a: Yes. A stove jack is just a closed port when not in use. These tents also work as regular camping tents in milder weather.

faq.q: How many people really fit with a stove?
faq.a: Usually about half the label. A tent rated for four is comfortable for two plus a stove and firewood. Size up if you expect to cook or dry gear inside.
